title: Treasury International Capital (TIC) monthly release (December 2026 data) — the first ordinary edition after the January annual revision, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: EST: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,181 bytes) by the tic-monthly-2027-01-19 initial-research adjacency sweep — its 2027 table's February row reads '18' in the Monthly column and '26 - prelim.' in the separate annual-survey column, under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'. Reference month December 2026 by the page's own 1.5-month lag rule. Corroborated mechanically: with the 5 U.S.C. 6103 federal holidays excluded (Presidents' Day 2027-02-15) the 11th business day of February 2027 is 2027-02-16, putting the published date at offset +2 business days, inside the page's own '11th business day plus 0 to 3 days' rule — the same holiday-aware convention that lands in-window on 22 of the 24 published 2026-27 dates and hits 9 exactly, recomputed from scratch by this session rather than inherited. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep: the proposer may not confirm what it found, only the event's own session may. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the tic-monthly-2027-01-19 initial research (2026-09-09) from that event's own primary fetch of Treasury's release-dates page. Proposed as THE NEXT UNCLAIMED SLOT: 2027-01-19 is now canonical and every earlier TIC date on this calendar is already owned, so this sweep proposes the first slot nobody holds rather than duplicating one (a second proposal for an owned id is a competing proposal the validator warns on). It also has a specific job. This session measured, for the first time in this series, that Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct revision editions restate an overlapping monthly cell by a mean $5.01bn against $1.67bn for an ordinary edition (t=+3.93, n=6 vs 10, February/March vintages excluded as a separate and larger benchmark mechanism). 2027-02-18 is the ORDINARY edition standing immediately after 2027-01-19's revision edition, so it is the control observation that test needs: the same diff run one month later, against a vintage the annual revision has already passed through. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds (16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is six weeks stale, no house playbook is macro-keyed). Note that 2027-02-18 sits in the same week as the 2027-02-26 preliminary annual survey proposed alongside it, whose benchmark feed this session found to be the largest single restatement in the whole vintage panel — the two are worth reading together. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
